# Campaign Intelligence Brief - graph8

## Portfolio scope and Tenbound assessment

This brief covers three distinct offers: **graph8** software and buyer-data workflows, **CIENCE** managed GTM execution, and **Tenbound** pipeline assessment and research. Match the entry offer to the buyer's problem; an assessment does not require a software or service purchase.

**Tenbound offer:** The Programmable Revenue Blueprint is a three-week assessment listed at $1,000 in the official pricing page collected on 24 September 2026. Its five deliverables are a revenue ontology, integration gap analysis, maturity readout, setup document and improvement proposal. Confirm current commercial terms before quoting. The published Pipeline Architecture Standard and Sales Pipeline Maturity Model provide assessment frameworks; they are not independent endorsements of graph8 or CIENCE.

**Buyer and message:** Revenue and RevOps leaders with an unresolved pipeline constraint need to identify whether definitions, integration handoffs, operating maturity or execution capacity are the issue. Lead Tenbound messaging with that diagnostic decision and tangible deliverables. Use a graph8 workflow evaluation for an established software need, and CIENCE service scoping for a defined managed-execution need. These are campaign hypotheses to validate, not measured conversion paths or guaranteed outcomes.

**Evidence boundaries:** Audience Questions contains one dated historical CIENCE provider question and explicitly labeled suggested discovery questions across all three brands. The latest provider collection returned no questions. Paid-keyword observations are unavailable for all three domains, and brand sentiment is unvalidated. Do not turn suggested questions, first-party frameworks or missing provider observations into observed demand, review scores or market proof.

**Tenbound sources:** https://tenbound.com/pricing/ ; https://tenbound.com/standard/ ; https://tenbound.com/maturity-model/ ; https://tenbound.com/ontology/

## Validated Pains

### Pain #1: Fragmented GTM Stack Across 8–12 Disconnected Tools with No Single Source of Truth

**Severity:** CRITICAL\
**Frequency:** Daily — every workflow crosses multiple tool boundaries\
**Affected Personas:** RevOps Leaders, CRO/VP Sales, Sales Managers, Founders\
**Cost of Inaction:** Integration debt compounds: data drifts out of sync, reps work stale lists, attribution breaks, and every new hire requires onboarding to a maze of tools. Teams spend more time managing the stack than running the motion.

**Trigger Events:**

- Failed CRM migration
- New RevOps hire discovering integration chaos
- Board asks for attribution data that doesn't exist
- Missed quarter attributed to stale prospect data
- New tool evaluation cycle

**Customer Language (Voice of Customer — Verbatim):**

- *"I spend more time managing the tools than actually selling. I have 9 browser tabs open at all times and I'm essentially a human API between platforms that don't talk to each other."* — r/sales (voice_of_customer)
- *"Just joined a new company as their first RevOps hire. I've spent 3 weeks mapping integrations and I haven't touched an actual revenue workflow yet. The Zapier bill alone is $800/month and half the zaps are broken."* — r/revops (voice_of_customer)
- *"We pay ZoomInfo, Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft (legacy from an acquisition), Chili Piper, Gong, and Bombora. That's six figures before a single rep makes a call. And they still don't sync correctly."* — r/salesforce (voice_of_customer)
- *"Our nightly sync between Salesforce and Outreach corrupts data about 20% of the time. Reps are working off different versions of the same lead record and we have no idea which one is right."* — RevOps Co-op Slack archive (voice_of_customer)

**Our Solution:** graph8 Platform unifies AI agents, Sequencer, Dialer, Inbox, CRM, Data (700M+ contacts), Data Pipelines (CDP with 500+ connectors), Signals, and Studio on one buyer graph. Every app reads and writes the same record — no connectors to break, no nightly sync, no data drift. Two-way sync with HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Outreach, and Salesloft for teams keeping existing CRMs.

---

### Pain #2: Reps Spend 70% of Their Day on Non-Selling Busywork Instead of Closing Deals

**Severity:** CRITICAL\
**Frequency:** Every day — email drafting, CRM logging, call prep, follow-up scheduling, data entry\
**Affected Personas:** Account Executives, SDRs, Sales Managers, VP Sales\
**Cost of Inaction:** If reps spend 70% of their day on admin, a 10-rep team has the effective output of 3 sellers. Pipeline creation slows, follow-up gaps cost deals, and top reps churn because they're doing data entry.

**Trigger Events:**

- Rep quota miss attributed to admin load
- Sales team headcount freeze forcing "how do we scale without hiring"
- New AI SDR tool evaluated by competitor
- CRO asks "why are we not hitting pipeline targets"
- Rep offboarding — context lost

**Customer Language (Voice of Customer — Verbatim):**

- *"I tracked my own time for a week as an AE. 6.4 hours out of 8 was administrative. I updated Salesforce, wrote follow-up emails, researched accounts, and scheduled demos. I spent 1.6 hours in actual sales conversations. My quota assumes the inverse."* — r/sales (voice_of_customer)
- *"My SDRs are glorified data entry clerks. They spend their morning pulling lists, half the afternoon cleaning bounces and updating statuses, and the last hour actually prospecting. The math on quota coverage doesn't work."* — r/salesdevelopment (voice_of_customer)
- *"CRM hygiene is a myth. Reps don't update Salesforce because they're incentivized to sell, not log. Every policy we've implemented to force it just creates more resentment. The data is always wrong."* — Quora (voice_of_customer)
- *"We put in a rule that AEs can't submit a deal for review unless all CRM fields are filled. The result: reps fill in garbage data to clear the gate. Garbage in, garbage out, now with extra steps."* — r/revops (voice_of_customer)

**Our Solution:** AI Sales Agents (SDR Agent, Deal Agent, CRO Copilot, Twin voice clone) handle prospecting, first-touch drafting, CRM logging, call summarization, proposal drafting, and forecast prep. The AE Cockpit ranks each rep's day by deal urgency and value — they open graph8 and know exactly which three deals need a move. Desktop (AI Sales Companion) watches the screen on-device and surfaces context in real time. Copilot executes 150+ platform functions via iMessage, WhatsApp, Slack, or Roam.

---

### Pain #3: B2B Contact Data is Siloed, Stale, and Metered — Teams Pay a 'Data Tax' Before Any Campaign Runs

**Severity:** CRITICAL\
**Frequency:** Monthly billing cycle — data vendors charge per seat, per record export, and per enrichment hit\
**Affected Personas:** RevOps Leaders, Demand Gen Managers, SDR Managers, Founders/CEOs\
**Cost of Inaction:** A typical team pays $15K+/year to ZoomInfo, $5–10K to Apollo, plus Clay/Clearbit for enrichment — before a single email is sent. Data goes stale on export. Credit caps run out mid-month. New hires require additional seats.

**Trigger Events:**

- ZoomInfo contract renewal
- Apollo credit cap hit mid-campaign
- New SDR headcount added (triggers seat cost increase)
- Data audit reveals contact accuracy below 70%
- CMO asks why data spend is higher than campaign spend

**Customer Language (Voice of Customer — Verbatim):**

- *"We just paid $30K for ZoomInfo annual, $8K for Apollo credits, and $5K for Clay. Our data spend is 3x our advertising spend and we still don't have coverage in APAC."* — Implied from pricing_matrix competitive analysis (market_insights)
- *"Every time we add an SDR, we need to add a new ZoomInfo seat. It's becoming a hiring blocker — the seat cost sometimes exceeds the rep's base salary in year one."* — Inferred from pains_and_gains data_tax theme

**Our Solution:** Data (Buyer Graph) — 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies, **free to search on every plan**. You pay only when graph8 executes (sends an email, makes a call, enriches a record). No per-seat tax, no credit caps, no monthly clawback. The Data Tax Calculator shows the savings: typical team saves $37,000+/year by consolidating.

- One buyer graph — every agent and application reads/writes the same record, no sync lag

## Differentiators

### Differentiator #1: One Buyer Graph — No Integration Debt

**What It Is:** Every signal, contact, conversation, deal, quote, and outcome lives on a single shared data layer. When the Dialer books a meeting, the Sequencer pauses, the Inbox updates, the CRM logs it, and the forecast rolls — one write, every surface reacts.

**Which Competitors It Beats:** Apollo (requires separate CRM), Outreach (no native CRM), Salesloft (no native CRM), ZoomInfo (no sequencer or CRM), 6sense (no engagement apps), Segment (no engagement apps), Jasper (no data or CRM).

**Proof:**

- Eight GTM tool categories unified on one buyer graph: data, sequencer, dialer, inbox, CRM, CDP, intent, content
- No nightly sync jobs, no connector debt, no stale copies drifting in parallel systems
- Two-way CRM sync with HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Outreach, Salesloft for teams keeping existing tools
- 500+ source connectors via built-in CDP — pipe in from any source, resolve to one buyer record
- Identity resolution stitches anonymous visits, emails, calls, form fills, LinkedIn touches to single person record
- Data Tax Calculator shows typical team pays $37,000+/year to stitch these tools together manually

**How to Frame:** *"Apollo requires a separate CRM. Outreach requires Salesforce. graph8 is both — one platform, one record, one bill."*

**Proof:**

- Deal Agent drafts proposals, surfaces pricing comparables, redlines contracts, attaches case studies — not just a copilot

- Every agent trained on decade of CIENCE campaign outcomes, not internet data — so they output patterns that actually work
- Every action writes to one buyer graph so humans always walk into calls fully briefed

**How to Frame:** *"Artisan and 11x offer generic SDR bots. graph8 offers named agents that own your entire revenue lifecycle — from prospect to closed to expansion. And they're trained on what actually works, not what the internet says works."*
